story: Feature: Authorize an operational recovery effect
As a cloud operations manager
I want a reviewable permission decision for a particular cloud change
So that a model suggestion or operator click cannot bypass the admitted effect boundary
sfx-aws-authorize-remediation.rule: Rule: The circuit yields an attributable outcome without assuming missing AWS proof
sfx-aws-authorize-remediation.given: Given a proposed recovery effect, target and trusted operator context
sfx-aws-authorize-remediation.when: When the effect-specific authority and approval requirements are evaluated
sfx-aws-authorize-remediation.then: Then an authorized effect or an explicit pending or refused disposition is available

story: Feature: Correlate infrastructure change evidence
As a incident investigator
I want historical change evidence relevant to an affected resource
So that the team distinguishes observed change from a causal hypothesis
sfx-aws-correlate-change-evidence.rule: Rule: The circuit yields an attributable outcome without assuming missing AWS proof
sfx-aws-correlate-change-evidence.given: Given a scoped resource and incident observation window
sfx-aws-correlate-change-evidence.when: When AWS change evidence is correlated without assuming causation
sfx-aws-correlate-change-evidence.then: Then a bounded change-evidence finding or an explicit evidence gap is available

story: Feature: Dispatch an approved AWS Automation runbook
As a incident responder
I want one attributable execution of an explicitly admitted runbook
So that recovery is delegated to an AWS native operator under precise permission and idempotency
sfx-aws-dispatch-approved-automation.rule: Rule: The circuit yields an attributable outcome without assuming missing AWS proof
sfx-aws-dispatch-approved-automation.given: Given one authorized recovery effect and an immutable runbook binding
sfx-aws-dispatch-approved-automation.when: When the bounded AWS Automation dispatch is attempted
sfx-aws-dispatch-approved-automation.then: Then the automation execution is addressable or a named non-dispatch prevents effect

story: Feature: Observe a cloud operational signal
As a cloud operations team
I want one bounded operational condition from an authenticated source
So that investigation begins with a traceable observation rather than an unverified alert
sfx-aws-observe-operational-signal.rule: Rule: The circuit yields an attributable outcome without assuming missing AWS proof
sfx-aws-observe-operational-signal.given: Given an AWS operational event and its attributed delivery context
sfx-aws-observe-operational-signal.when: When the operational event is checked and admitted
sfx-aws-observe-operational-signal.then: Then a distinct qualified signal is observable, or the event is safely classified

story: Feature: Resolve affected AWS resource context
As a cloud operations engineer
I want the ownership and current condition of a cloud resource
So that the team can target the correct account, environment and service without guessing
sfx-aws-resolve-resource-context.rule: Rule: The circuit yields an attributable outcome without assuming missing AWS proof
sfx-aws-resolve-resource-context.given: Given an admitted operational signal and an AWS resource identity
sfx-aws-resolve-resource-context.when: When the governed resource context is resolved
sfx-aws-resolve-resource-context.then: Then one attributable resource context or a named coverage limitation is available

story: Feature: Assess operational service impact
As a cloud operations manager
I want an attributable view of service degradation and its coverage
So that incident priority reflects service effect rather than alarm count
sfx-aws-resolve-service-impact.rule: Rule: The circuit yields an attributable outcome without assuming missing AWS proof
sfx-aws-resolve-service-impact.given: Given a qualified signal, service binding and reliability evidence
sfx-aws-resolve-service-impact.when: When the service impact is assessed against its declared operating objective
sfx-aws-resolve-service-impact.then: Then the observed service impact or its unobservability is stated

story: Feature: Resolve a cloud service incident through governed AWS capabilities
As a cloud operations manager
I want a service incident either recovered with proof or safely escalated
So that every action, constraint and unresolved condition is visible in one incident circuit
sfx-aws-resolve-service-incident.rule: Rule: The circuit yields an attributable outcome without assuming missing AWS proof
sfx-aws-resolve-service-incident.given: Given one qualified cloud incident with its admitted service and effect boundary
sfx-aws-resolve-service-incident.when: When the admitted investigation, response and recovery circuits are composed
sfx-aws-resolve-service-incident.then: Then the service is independently restored, or the incident retains an explicit non-restored disposition

story: Feature: Select a governed recovery option
As a on-call cloud operator
I want a permitted action matched to the observed cloud condition
So that remediation options follow the resource state and approved runbook policy
sfx-aws-select-recovery-option.rule: Rule: The circuit yields an attributable outcome without assuming missing AWS proof
sfx-aws-select-recovery-option.given: Given an incident assessment and admitted runbook catalog
sfx-aws-select-recovery-option.when: When one eligible bounded recovery option is selected
sfx-aws-select-recovery-option.then: Then an eligible action is available, or the incident is left for manual escalation

story: Feature: Verify a cloud service recovery from independent observations
As a cloud operations manager
I want proof that the operational experience has recovered
So that a successful automation invocation never substitutes for a healthy service
sfx-aws-verify-service-recovery.rule: Rule: The circuit yields an attributable outcome without assuming missing AWS proof
sfx-aws-verify-service-recovery.given: Given an automation result and a declared post-action service objective
sfx-aws-verify-service-recovery.when: When the current service state is independently checked against the objective
sfx-aws-verify-service-recovery.then: Then recovery is confirmed, rejected, or left unobservable with evidence

story: Feature: Assess cloud configuration against governed expectations
As a cloud governance owner
I want a reviewable difference between intended and observed cloud resources
So that configuration drift is interpreted from facts rather than a stale deployment diagram
sfx-aws-assess-configuration-drift.rule: Rule: The circuit yields an attributable outcome without assuming missing AWS proof
sfx-aws-assess-configuration-drift.given: Given a declared resource policy and AWS configuration observation
sfx-aws-assess-configuration-drift.when: When the observed configuration is evaluated against its admitted target
sfx-aws-assess-configuration-drift.then: Then a specific drift finding, no drift, or a coverage limitation is available

story: Feature: Assess AWS spend against an admitted budget or baseline
As a cloud financial operations owner
I want a cost change that is measurable and attributed to a defined scope
So that cost optimization begins from spend evidence rather than speculative savings
sfx-aws-assess-cost-variance.rule: Rule: The circuit yields an attributable outcome without assuming missing AWS proof
sfx-aws-assess-cost-variance.given: Given a billing scope, comparison period and AWS cost observation
sfx-aws-assess-cost-variance.when: When the scoped cost evidence is compared under a declared variance rule
sfx-aws-assess-cost-variance.then: Then an attributable variance or an explicit coverage limitation is available

story: Feature: Evaluate recovery readiness for a cloud workload
As a service continuity owner
I want an evidence-based view of recovery preparedness
So that a backup configured does not by itself prove recoverability
sfx-aws-evaluate-recovery-readiness.rule: Rule: The circuit yields an attributable outcome without assuming missing AWS proof
sfx-aws-evaluate-recovery-readiness.given: Given a recovery obligation and its actual backup or exercise evidence
sfx-aws-evaluate-recovery-readiness.when: When the observed recovery controls are checked against the declared recovery objective
sfx-aws-evaluate-recovery-readiness.then: Then a supported readiness disposition with exact gaps is available

story: Feature: Report AWS cloud operations posture
As a cloud operations manager
I want a credible operating picture across reliability, security, cost and recovery
So that leadership can see which obligations are met and which are not yet observable
sfx-aws-report-operating-posture.rule: Rule: The circuit yields an attributable outcome without assuming missing AWS proof
sfx-aws-report-operating-posture.given: Given a scoped estate window with admitted operational evidence
sfx-aws-report-operating-posture.when: When the collected operational findings are assembled without hiding gaps
sfx-aws-report-operating-posture.then: Then a reviewable operating posture report or explicit incomplete disposition is available

story: Feature: Triage an AWS security finding with attributable evidence
As a security operations manager
I want a prioritized cloud-security observation with safe next action
So that findings are not mistaken for automatically authorized remediations
sfx-aws-triage-security-finding.rule: Rule: The circuit yields an attributable outcome without assuming missing AWS proof
sfx-aws-triage-security-finding.given: Given a supported AWS Security Hub finding and authorized security scope
sfx-aws-triage-security-finding.when: When the finding is deduplicated and classified against approved policy
sfx-aws-triage-security-finding.then: Then an owned security work item is available or a named non-admission explains the absence
